title: Coast Guard and Navy Train for Search and Rescue
description: Package of the Coast Guard Cutter Washington conducting search and rescue training with Navy SH-60B helicopter from Navy Helicopter Sea Combat Squadron 25 in Agat Bay,Guam. HSC-25 helicopter's regularly assist in Sector Guam's remote area of responsibility for the search and rescue missions. Produced by Lt. j.g. Justin Valentino.
keywords: HSC-25, District 14, Search and rescue training, Justin Valentino, agat bay, Coast Guard Cutter Washington, Coast Guard, navy, Guam

transcript.text: Around the nation and around the world, the United States Coast Guard stands ready to conduct a wide variety of missions, including law enforcement and search and rescue.
On the island of Guam, the remote U.S. territory in the western Pacific, the United States Coast Guard, Washington prepares to get underway to exercise its missions.
The Coast Guard, Washington regularly conducts drills and exercises which prepare the crew to conduct their missions.
Due to the lack of Coast Guard air assets in Guam, U.S. Coast Guard relies on close inter-agency support with our DOD partners.
One of the more unique drills they conduct is flight operations with a helicopter.
For over three decades, the Navy helicopter seeks combat swag in 25, and assisted the U.S. Coast Guard in conducting the search and rescue mission in Guam.

As they are the only helicopter assets capable of this mission, these partnerships are closely exercised and practiced routinely in order to ensure a safe and effective partnership which helps support the people of Guam and the Northern Marianna faculty.
These exercises included the boosting operations which practice lifting patients from the deck of the cutter using the basket voice from the helicopter.
With the exercise complete, the helicopter from Navy HSC-55 returns home. The cutter continues on its patrol, ready to support the people of Guam.
